content:
Hi all, first post here. I wanted to share an industrial Lean 4 use case, and ask whether I've drawn the trust boundary sensibly.

I built bitrep, an open-source Rust crate for order-invariant, bit-identical floating-point reductions (a Kulisch-style fixed-point superaccumulator with a canonical 289-byte encoding, aimed at distributed aggregation, float counter CRDTs, and signable statistics).

The Lean side proves: the merge algebra (commutativity, associativity, merge-tree and permutation invariance of exact accumulation), the rounding kernel (round-to-nearest-ties-to-even, in full), the CRDT convergence laws, and the v0.2 toolkit's merge algebra for keyed maps, products, min/max joins, and saturating counters. Zero sorry, and CI runs an axiom audit on every push.

The gap between the Lean spec and the Rust implementation is bridged separately: Kani/CBMC model-checks that the implemented merges commute/associate and the codecs round-trip, plus differential fuzzing against a big-integer oracle. I state this boundary explicitly rather than claiming the Rust code itself is verified.

Questions I'd value input on:

  1. Is the axiom audit (checking the proofs depend only on the expected axioms) the right hygiene here, or is there a stronger standard the community uses for "proofs you can trust in CI"?
  2. Has anyone connected Lean specs to Rust implementations more directly than the Kani-as-bridge approach? I'd love to shrink that gap.

Proofs are in the repo: https://github.com/KyleClouthier/bitrep (lean/ directory). There's also a browser demo that runs the cross-architecture reference test on your device: https://simgen.dev/bitrep

Thanks Snir, that page is exactly what I was hoping existed.

Good news on the mechanical items: the CI audit already does what it prescribes. Proofs build with lake on every push, and the check script runs #print axioms on every named theorem and fails unless the output is a subset of {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound} or empty. So "zero sorry" there is backed by the build and the axiom gate, not just a grep.

The page's harder point is well taken though: none of that certifies that the statements say what I claim they say. That part needs expert eyes, and honestly it's half of why I posted here. If anyone is willing to skim the theorem statements and tell me whether they correspond to the claims (order/merge-tree/permutation invariance of exact accumulation, round-to-nearest-ties-to-even, CRDT convergence), I'd genuinely welcome it, including the "your statement is vacuous or weaker than advertised" outcome. They're in the proofs/ directory (I said lean/ in my first message, my mistake): https://github.com/KyleClouthier/bitrep/tree/main/proofs

I'll dig into #comparator as well, thanks for the pointer.

Follow-up: comparator is now in CI. proofs/comparator/Challenge.lean is a self-contained spec (the model definitions plus all 34 theorem statements, sorried), and on every push the comparator verifies the real proofs prove exactly those statements with only the standard axiom base, kernel-replayed. CI also asserts the solution file is byte-for-byte the four proof files, so the spec can't drift from what's actually checked. That shrinks my original question nicely: a reviewer now only needs to read Challenge.lean. Thanks again for the pointer — this was exactly the missing piece.

https://github.com/KyleClouthier/bitrep/tree/main/proofs/comparator
Alongside the "Did you prove it?" reference that Snir mentioned, the lean reference manual has a page on Validating a Lean Proof that discusses comparator.

I had a very fast glance, but I would immediately say that the AI needs to be told to use as much API from mathlib as it can do make checking easier. For example in main/proofs/FloatGCounter.lean:

def ejoin (a b : Nat) : Nat := Nat.max a b

theorem ejoin_comm (a b : Nat) : ejoin a b = ejoin b a :=
  Nat.max_comm a b

theorem ejoin_assoc (a b c : Nat) :
    ejoin (ejoin a b) c = ejoin a (ejoin b c) :=
  Nat.max_assoc a b c

theorem ejoin_idem (a : Nat) : ejoin a a = a :=
  Nat.max_self a

But we have docs#Nat.max_comm, docs#Nat.max_assoc and docs#Nat.max_self on their own, there isn't a need to do these, just makes it much harder to check unfortunately jumping through such hoops.

Done, thanks for the nudge Yan. Dropped the three ejoin_comm/assoc/idem wrappers, and join_comm/assoc/idem now defer straight to Nat.max_comm/assoc/self. Kept the ejoin def since join is defined pointwise over it and it's defeq Nat.max anyway, but the redundant restatements are gone. Fewer hoops to check now. Comparator's still green and the axiom audit is unchanged. Appretiate the input!

@Rob Simmons Thanks Rob, that's a great pointer. Comparator's actually already wired into the CI here, it re-checks on every push that the proofs prove exactly the statements in one self-contained spec file (proofs/comparator/), so a reviewer only has to read that one file. That reference page explains the why more cleanly than I've been managing to, I'll link it from the repo.
